instruction: Run a speed test on speedtest.net and save the full results, including ISP details, to ~/Documents/connection_report.txt.

metadata.explanation: Task requires running a speed test on speedtest.net and exporting comprehensive results including ISP information. The evaluator checks if connection_report.txt in Documents contains Download, Upload metrics and ISP information, ensuring the user completed the test and saved complete network details.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary scoring: 1.0 if all required keywords (Download, Upload, ISP) are present in the file, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is fundamentally sound - getter correctly fetches the file from expected location and metric checks for relevant keywords
Good semantic alignment - checking for 'Download', 'Upload', 'ISP' keywords reasonably verifies that speed test results with ISP info were exported
Coverage is adequate - the three keywords cover the main requirements (speed metrics + ISP information)
Case-sensitive keyword matching could cause false negatives if speedtest.net uses different capitalization (e.g., 'download' vs 'Download')
Keyword matching is somewhat brittle - speedtest.net might format results differently (e.g., 'Download Speed:', 'DL:', 'Internet Service Provider' instead of exact keywords)
No validation that keywords appear in meaningful context - they could theoretically appear in headers/instructions rather than actual results
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making keyword matching case-insensitive by converting file_text to lowercase before checking
Consider using more flexible keyword matching (e.g., checking if 'download' appears anywhere in lowercase text, or using regex patterns)
Optionally add checks for presence of numeric values near keywords to ensure actual test results are present (not just labels)
